name: HubspotMCP
title: HubSpot
description: Resolve the signed-in user to their HubSpot contact and output that profile; an attached agent can also read it and push insight notes back.
whenToUse: Pick to ground a conversation in the signed-in customer. It resolves the logged-in user (by their authenticated email) to their HubSpot contact and emits that identity profile, so downstream steps start already knowing who they are talking to. Wire it inline (trigger to contact profile out) to use the lookup as a step, or attach it via a service edge to an agent, which can also append a durable insight note to the contact. The user is read from the session, never from the input.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger to fire the node. Carries no lookup data: the user is resolved from the session, not from this input.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The signed-in user's bounded contact profile { ok, found, contact }. `contact` is null when the user is not in the CRM, which is a normal result and not an error.

syncUser.title: Sync user on trigger
syncUser.description: On trigger, drain any insight notes the memory server has queued for this contact and write them to the CRM. Leave off for a plain lookup that just outputs the contact. The identity snapshot is refreshed either way.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: hubspot
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. This package is `package.yaml`, `nodes/`, `credentials/` and
# `shared/`, and nothing else: no src/, no package.json, no build, no npm publish.
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/hubspot/`, whose README maps each file to
# what replaced it.
#
# Retiring the code is what SWITCHED IT ON. A code node of the same type beats a
# manifest at load, so while src/index.ts still called api.registerNode the manifests
# were parsed and skipped. `@unoverse-platform/hubspot` is also uninstalled from the
# plugins volume, and plugins/startup.ts skips an npm copy whenever a folder of that
# name exists here, so a published copy in some universe cannot climb back in.
#
# `config.syncUser` is BACK. It was lost when the code was retired, because it reached
# Redis rather than an HTTP host; the executor now names `state` operations, so the
# snapshot and the hydrate outbox are expressed here like everything else.
#
# Still NOT restored: the dictionary attribute pull, which scored dictionary entries
# against HubSpot's property catalog. That is computation rather than description, and it
# belongs in the executor as a named capability or nowhere. See
# _legacy/nodes/hubspot/README.md.

name: hubspot
displayName: HubSpot
description: HubSpot CRM integration for Unoverse
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1784461921/gravity/icons/Hubspot.svg

features:
  - Resolve the signed-in user to their CRM contact
  - Append machine-authored insight notes to a contact

# The ONLY hosts this package's nodes may call. The executor refuses anything else.
#
# A manifest cannot execute code, but without this it could still say "send this
# credential to evil.example", which is exfiltration with no code at all.
allowedHosts:
  - api.hubapi.com

# Executor capabilities every manifest node here depends on. Deploy REFUSES this
# package if the target universe's executor cannot satisfy them.
requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  state: [read, merge, drain]
  executorVersion: ">=1.1.0"

credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from src/credentials/index.ts.
#
# A HubSpot Service Key IS the bearer token: unlike Salesforce there is no OAuth2
# exchange step, which is why this node needs only the one field and the `bearer`
# scheme the executor already implements.
#
# Nodes reference this BY NAME. The retired executor picked its credential by scanning
# the bag for the first object with an `accessToken`, which silently authenticates
# against the wrong service the moment a second such credential joins the workflow
# (04-credentials.md). The manifest names it, so that class of bug cannot recur.

name: hubspotPrivateApp
displayName: HubSpot
description: >-
  HubSpot Service Key. Create one in HubSpot scoped to crm.objects.contacts read/write
  and crm.objects.notes read/write, then paste it here. Add crm.objects.companies.read
  to resolve a contact's company when it lives on an associated Company record.
documentationUrl: https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api/private-apps

properties:
  - name: accessToken
    displayName: Service Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your HubSpot Service Key (sent as the API bearer token)
    placeholder: pat-

shared.contact.yaml:
# Resolving the signed-in person to a HubSpot contact, refreshing the snapshot the memory
# server reads, and the bounded profile that comes back.
#
# Every call is a named top-level key with a YAML anchor, and the lists below compose them.
# That is what lets `write_contact_meta` reuse the search alone without also following
# company associations it has no use for, while the two read paths share every call.

# ── the calls ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The node's own last snapshot, read back so the WORKFLOW channel can skip HubSpot while it
# is fresh. Freshness is judged on `syncedAt`, which only the cache call below writes:
# `updatedAt` is stamped by EVERY merge to this key, including the memory server's, so a
# busy memory lane would keep it looking fresh and the sync would never run again.
snapshot: &snapshot
  name: snapshot
  state: read
  when: "return !!scope.userId && !!scope.workflowId"
  key: "crm:{{ scope.userId }}:{{ scope.workflowId }}"

# The email is the join key, and it comes from the SESSION, not the wire. A caller may name
# one (an agent asking about a colleague), and with no caller `params` is empty, so the
# workflow channel always resolves the signed-in user and cannot be steered onto someone
# else's record by an upstream node.
search: &search
  name: search
  # NO EMAIL, NO CALL. The retired code returned a structured "nothing to resolve" result
  # here rather than calling HubSpot, and dropping that guard sent a filter with no value,
  # which HubSpot rejects as invalid JSON. That is the wrong error in the wrong place: the
  # node cannot resolve a person nobody named, and it should say so itself.
  #
  # It happens for real: the node tester has no signed-in session, so `user.email` is empty
  # unless a caller passes one.
  when: "return !!(params.email || user.email)"
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: endpoints#contactSearch }
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
  body: >-
    return {
      filterGroups: [{ filters: [{
        propertyName: 'email',
        operator: 'EQ',
        value: params.email || user.email
      }] }],
      properties: ['firstname', 'lastname', 'email', 'phone', 'jobtitle', 'company', 'lifecyclestage'],
      limit: 1
    }
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# The search the SYNC sequence runs: identical to `search` except it also stands down while
# the snapshot is fresh. The 10 minutes is MEMORY_SPEC.md's number for this snapshot
# (cache-aside, 10-min TTL) — the retired executor carried it as a Redis TTL, which the
# shared state key can no longer do (the memory server merges into it), so the freshness
# window moved onto the sync's own stamp. A duplicate rather than a merge key because the
# YAML loader parses 1.2, which has no `<<`. The `name` stays `search` so every downstream
# `calls.search` gate works unchanged; only the sync sequence carries a snapshot call, so
# only it can skip.
#
# The service tools deliberately do NOT use this: `write_contact_meta` attaches a note by
# the id of a LIVE search, and `get_contact` answers a direct question, where a stale reply
# is a lie rather than a saving.
syncSearch: &syncSearch
  name: search
  when: >-
    return !!(params.email || user.email) && (
      !!params.email
      || !((calls.snapshot || {}).syncedAt)
      || (Date.now() - (calls.snapshot || {}).syncedAt) > 10 * 60 * 1000
    )
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: endpoints#contactSearch }
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
  body: >-
    return {
      filterGroups: [{ filters: [{
        propertyName: 'email',
        operator: 'EQ',
        value: params.email || user.email
      }] }],
      properties: ['firstname', 'lastname', 'email', 'phone', 'jobtitle', 'company', 'lifecyclestage'],
      limit: 1
    }
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# A contact's company usually lives on an ASSOCIATED Company record rather than in the
# contact's own `company` text property, so this runs only when that property came back
# blank. A skipped call leaves no key, which is what the next one's `when` tests.
association: &association
  name: association
  when: "return (((calls.search || {}).results) || []).filter(c => !c.properties.company).length > 0"
  method: GET
  url: "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts/{{ calls.search.results.[0].id }}/associations/companies"
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
  query:
    limit: "1"
  transport: json

# v3 associations name the related record `toObjectId` for some object pairs and `id` for
# others, which is why the retired code wrote `toObjectId ?? id`. An expression url can say
# it; a Handlebars one could not, and an earlier draft moved the whole thing to v4 just to
# dodge that. The node should not bend around a limitation of the executor.
company: &company
  name: company
  when: "return ((calls.association || {}).results || []).length > 0"
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/companies/'
      + (calls.association.results[0].toObjectId || calls.association.results[0].id)
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
  query:
    properties: name
  transport: json

# The identity snapshot the memory server reads, at `crm:{userId}:{workflowId}`. The
# retired executor wrote this on EVERY path, so the dashboard stayed warm for free.
#
# MERGE, not replace: the memory server writes its own fields into the same key, and a
# wholesale write would drop them. Skipped outside a workflow (the bench, an ad-hoc call),
# where there is no scope to key on.
cache: &cache
  name: cache
  state: merge
  # Needs a workflow to key on AND a search that actually ran: caching "no contact" when
  # nobody was even named would write a cold miss over a warm snapshot.
  when: "return !!scope.userId && !!scope.workflowId && !!calls.search"
  key: "crm:{{ scope.userId }}:{{ scope.workflowId }}"
  # The FULL result allowlist, not a trimmed one: a sync turn that skips the search replays
  # this contact as its result, so anything the result promises must be here. `syncedAt` is
  # epoch millis (`new Date()` is unavailable in the sandbox, and rightly so) and is the
  # freshness stamp `syncSearch` reads; see the snapshot call for why `updatedAt` cannot
  # serve.
  value: >-
    return { syncedAt: Date.now(),
      contact: (((calls.search || {}).results) || []).map(c => ({
      id: c.id,
      name: [c.properties.firstname, c.properties.lastname].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || null,
      firstName: c.properties.firstname || null,
      lastName: c.properties.lastname || null,
      email: c.properties.email || null,
      phone: c.properties.phone || null,
      title: c.properties.jobtitle || null,
      company: c.properties.company || ((calls.company || {}).properties || {}).name || null,
      lifecycleStage: c.properties.lifecyclestage || null,
      kind: c.properties.lifecyclestage === 'customer' ? 'customer' : 'lead'
    }))[0] || null }

# Hydrate, the other direction: the memory server appends a high-certainty deduction to
# this queue, and the connector drains it into the CRM on the next conversation.
#
# Items are POPPED, so dedup is inherent and a re-run cannot duplicate a note. The cost of
# that is real and worth naming: if the batch write below fails, the drained items are
# already off the queue and are lost. The retired code had the same shape one item at a
# time, so this trades a smaller blast radius for 1 call instead of 25.
hydrate: &hydrate
  name: hydrate
  state: drain
  # A contact from EITHER source will do: the drain runs on every sync turn, including the
  # ones where a fresh snapshot skipped the search, so a queued deduction never waits out
  # the cache TTL before landing in the CRM.
  when: >-
    return config.syncUser === true && (
      (((calls.search || {}).results) || []).length > 0
      || !!(((calls.snapshot || {}).contact) || {}).id
    )
  key: "crm:hydrate:{{ scope.userId }}:{{ scope.workflowId }}"
  max: 25

# One BATCH create rather than a call per item. A manifest cannot loop a collection into N
# requests, and it does not need to: the vendor takes an array, so the whole drain lands in
# a single call built by one expression.
hydrateNotes: &hydrateNotes
  name: hydrateNotes
  when: "return (calls.hydrate || []).length > 0"
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: endpoints#notesBatch }
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
  body: >-
    return { inputs: calls.hydrate.filter(i => i && i.claim).map(i => ({
      properties: {
        hs_note_body: 'Gravity AI — machine-authored, unverified'
          + (i.certainty ? ' (certainty ' + Math.round(i.certainty * 100) + '%)' : '')
          + '\n\n' + i.claim,
        hs_timestamp: Date.now()
      },
      associations: [{
        to: { id: ((((calls.search || {}).results) || [])[0] || {}).id || (((calls.snapshot || {}).contact) || {}).id },
        types: [{ associationCategory: 'HUBSPOT_DEFINED', associationTypeId: 202 }]
      }]
    })) }
  transport: json

# ── the sequences ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Find the person and fill in their company. Used where the caller only wants the answer.
resolve: [*search, *association, *company]

# The same, then refresh the snapshot. This is what both READ paths use, because the old
# executor cached on every one of them.
resolveAndCache: [*search, *association, *company, *cache]

# The full workflow-channel sequence. With `syncUser` off it behaves exactly like
# resolveAndCache, because every state call and the hydrate write are gated on the toggle.
# The snapshot read leads and the search is the TTL-gated variant, so a sync within the
# last 10 minutes costs one Redis read instead of the HubSpot chain. Only this sequence
# carries the snapshot, so the READ paths are unchanged.
sync: [*snapshot, *syncSearch, *association, *company, *cache, *hydrate, *hydrateNotes]

# ── what a caller gets back ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A FIXED allowlist of properties, never a full record dump.
#
# Wrapped in a one-element array and mapped rather than naming the profile twice: the
# sandbox has no assignment by design, and the alternative is evaluating the whole
# projection once for `found` and again for `contact`.
#
# A miss is `found: false`, never an error. A person who is not in the CRM is the normal
# case, and an agent that treats it as a failure stops the conversation dead.
#
# `kind` is derived here rather than stored, so it cannot go stale against lifecyclestage.
result: >-
  return !calls.search
    ? (((calls.snapshot || {}).syncedAt)
      ? { ok: true, found: !!calls.snapshot.contact, cached: true, contact: calls.snapshot.contact || null }
      : { ok: false, found: false, contact: null,
          error: 'No email to resolve. In production this defaults to the authenticated user; in a debug run, pass the contact email explicitly.' })
    : [(((calls.search || {}).results) || []).map(c => ({
    id: c.id,
    name: [c.properties.firstname, c.properties.lastname].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || null,
    firstName: c.properties.firstname || null,
    lastName: c.properties.lastname || null,
    email: c.properties.email || null,
    phone: c.properties.phone || null,
    title: c.properties.jobtitle || null,
    company: c.properties.company || ((calls.company || {}).properties || {}).name || null,
    lifecycleStage: c.properties.lifecyclestage || null,
    kind: c.properties.lifecyclestage === 'customer' ? 'customer' : 'lead'
  }))[0] || null].map(p => ({ ok: true, found: !!p, contact: p }))[0]
shared.endpoints.yaml:
# HubSpot CRM v3. The legacy .ssi bundle this node descends from used the deprecated
# v1 endpoints; those were deliberately not ported and are not listed here.
#
# One place for every URL, so an API version bump is one file.

base: https://api.hubapi.com

contactSearch: https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts/search
notes: https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/notes
notesBatch: https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/notes/batch/create

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order. This node has one connector,
# so the whole of its outward behaviour is this single row.
#
# `from: response` fires once over the settled reply of the LAST step, with every step
# reachable as calls.<name>, which is what the projection below reads.

- emit: output
  from: response
  value: { $ref: contact#result }
files.api/run.yaml:
# The WORKFLOW channel: what this node does when the graph runs it.
#
# Four calls: find the contact, fill in its company, then refresh the identity snapshot the
# memory server reads. See shared/contact.yaml.
#
# The signed-in user is resolved from the session. There is no email input and no query, so
# an upstream node cannot point this at someone else's record.
$ref: contact#sync
files.api/service.yaml:
# The SERVICE channel: the two tools an attached agent gets.
#
# Deliberately tiny. Read the signed-in user, and append a note about them. No search, no
# other objects, no contact CRUD. Both resolve the authenticated user server-side, so a
# model cannot widen its own reach by choosing different arguments.
#
# These descriptions are what the model reads when deciding whether to call a tool, so
# they say what comes back and what "empty" means, not just what the tool does.

get_contact:
  description: >-
    Get a user's CRM contact, their bounded identity profile (name, email, title,
    company). Pass an email to look that person up; omit it to read the currently
    authenticated user, which is the default. Returns an empty result if the user is not
    in the CRM (for example, not signed in). That is normal, just proceed.
  calls: { $ref: contact#resolveAndCache }
  returns: { $ref: contact#result }

write_contact_meta:
  description: >-
    Append a durable, machine-authored insight about the signed-in user to their CRM
    contact as a timeline note. APPEND-ONLY: it never edits any existing field. Resolves
    the authenticated user automatically, so just pass the insight. Push only
    high-certainty conclusions.
  calls:
    # Find the contact first. The search only, not the whole resolve chain: a note is
    # attached by id, so following company associations would be two wasted calls.
    - { $ref: contact#search }

    - name: note
      # No contact means nothing to attach to. Skipping leaves no calls.note, which is
      # what `returns` below tests to answer NO_CONTACT rather than claiming success.
      when: "return (((calls.search || {}).results) || []).length > 0"
      method: POST
      url: { $ref: endpoints#notes }
      credential:
        scheme: bearer
        token: "{{ credentials.hubspotPrivateApp.accessToken }}"
      # The stamp is a WIRE MARKER, not prose: notes are read back by matching this
      # prefix, so its wording is fixed and must not be tidied.
      #
      # hs_timestamp as epoch millis, which HubSpot accepts and the sandbox can produce.
      # `new Date()` is unavailable there by design, and rightly so.
      #
      # associationTypeId 202 is HubSpot's own Note-to-Contact type.
      body: >-
        return {
          properties: {
            hs_note_body: 'Gravity AI — machine-authored, unverified'
              + (params.certainty ? ' (certainty ' + Math.round(params.certainty * 100) + '%)' : '')
              + '\n\n' + params.insight,
            hs_timestamp: Date.now()
          },
          associations: [{
            to: { id: (((calls.search || {}).results) || [])[0].id },
            types: [{ associationCategory: 'HUBSPOT_DEFINED', associationTypeId: 202 }]
          }]
        }
      transport: json

  # Three outcomes, and they are different problems: the note landed, there is no contact to
  # attach it to, or nobody was named in the first place. The last one is what happens with
  # no signed-in session, and reporting it as NO_CONTACT would send someone looking in the
  # CRM for a person who was never asked for.
  returns: >-
    return calls.note
      ? { ok: !!calls.note.id, id: calls.note.id || null }
      : !calls.search
        ? { ok: false, error: 'NO_USER',
            hint: 'No email to resolve. In production this defaults to the authenticated user; in a debug run, pass the contact email explicitly.' }
        : { ok: false, error: 'NO_CONTACT',
            hint: 'No CRM contact for the signed-in user, so there is nothing to attach the note to.' }
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    syncUser:
      type: boolean
      title: Sync user on trigger
      description: >-
        On trigger, drain any insight notes the memory server has queued for this contact
        and write them to the CRM. Leave off for a plain lookup that just outputs the
        contact. The identity snapshot is refreshed either way.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order": [syncUser]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: >-
      Trigger to fire the node. Carries no lookup data: the user is resolved from the
      session, not from this input.

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: >-
      The signed-in user's bounded contact profile { ok, found, contact }. `contact` is
      null when the user is not in the CRM, which is a normal result and not an error.

credentials:
  - name: hubspotPrivateApp
    required: true
    displayName: HubSpot

# This node PROVIDES tools to an attached agent (isService: true), the opposite of
# OpenAIStream's mcp connector, which consumes them.
serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [get_contact, write_contact_meta]
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: get_contact (read the signed-in user's, or a passed email's,
      contact) and write_contact_meta (append a durable insight note to the contact).
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: HubspotMCP
# Every call settles, and a chain of settling calls settles too. Nothing here streams
# and there is no CONTINUE port, so this is a PromiseNode.
kind: PromiseNode
name: HubSpot
category: Go To Market
color: "#FF7A59"
# Drawn as a service node: it is ATTACHED to an agent over a service edge, not wired in
# sequence, so the compact card is the honest shape.
template: service
description: >-
  Resolve the signed-in user to their HubSpot contact and output that profile; an
  attached agent can also read it and push insight notes back.
whenToUse: >
  Pick to ground a conversation in the signed-in customer. It resolves the logged-in user
  (by their authenticated email) to their HubSpot contact and emits that identity profile,
  so downstream steps start already knowing who they are talking to. Wire it inline
  (trigger to contact profile out) to use the lookup as a step, or attach it via a service
  edge to an agent, which can also append a durable insight note to the contact. The user
  is read from the session, never from the input.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable. A CRM record changes underneath us, and write_contact_meta has a side
  # effect that reuse would silently skip. isTrigger is omitted, since false says nothing.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# This node has no options, so the fixture is really about WHO is asking: the whole node
# is a function of the signed-in person's email.
#
# The workflow channel and `get_contact` run the SAME chain (shared/contact.yaml), so
# exercising one exercises both. `write_contact_meta` is deliberately not the fixture: it
# writes a real note to a real CRM record, and a bench that leaves litter behind stops
# being something anyone runs twice.
testData:
  config: {}

  inputs:
    input: {}

  # Stands in for the session. Change this to an email that exists in the HubSpot
  # portal your Service Key points at, or the run correctly reports found: false.
  user:
    email: gavinapayne@gmail.com

  expect:
    # A miss is a RESULT, not a failure, so the run is only wrong if the call itself did
    # not complete. Asserting found: true would tie the fixture to one portal's data.
    output: >-
      return output.output.ok === true
        && (output.output.contact === null
            || typeof output.output.contact.email === 'string')
